bilingual.notes: Kansas does not offer a bilingual-education teacher credential. Neither the KSDE 'Adding an Endorsement' page nor the Higher Education Teacher Preparation Standards index lists a bilingual endorsement; only an ESOL endorsement exists.

eld.notes: ESOL endorsement (K.A.R. 91-1-203, updated March 2023) is an add-on to an existing Kansas teaching license, with two pathways: Option 1 — complete a state-approved ESOL program at a Kansas IHE plus pass the state-approved ESOL content exam; Option 2 ('Test Plus') — complete state-approved ESOL content-specific coursework at an approved KS institution (e.g., FHSU ESOL 884/885; KU C&T 330/331/491 or 820/825; K-State EDCI 420/431 or 720/742; McPherson CI 428/628; Newman EDUC 6133/6113; Washburn ED 650/624; Wichita State CI 775) plus pass the ESOL content exam. Practicum is included in some institutional pathways (FHSU, KU) but is not a statewide regulatory requirement, so coded null.

sei.notes: Kansas has no statewide sheltered-English-instruction (SEI) mandate for all teachers. The Professional Education Standards (adopted 2015, revised 2016) embed EL-relevant competencies in Standard 2 (Learning Differences) — including 2.1.5PS on strategies for making content accessible to English language learners — but these are teacher-preparation program standards, not an SEI endorsement requirement.

history.title: Kansas adopts revised Professional Education Teacher Preparation Standards
history.description: KSBE adopted Kansas's current Professional Education Teacher Preparation Standards on 2015-01-13. Standard 2 (Learning Differences) embeds EL-relevant competencies (e.g., 2.1.5PS — strategies for making content accessible to English language learners) into the general preparation framework that binds all Kansas-prepared teachers.

history.title: Professional Education Standards updated to add ESOL/virtual-learning content
history.description: KSBE edited the Professional Education Teacher Preparation Standards on 2016-04-29 to make ESOL and virtual-learning competencies explicit within the general preparation document. This is the textual basis for `professionalStandardsMentions.el = true` on Kansas's record.

history.title: Kansas adopts State Seal of Biliteracy
history.description: Kansas formally adopted a State Seal of Biliteracy program in 2016, recognizing high-school graduates proficient in English plus one or more world languages. KSDE publishes program guidance; participation is district-opt-in.

history.title: KSBE adopts ESOL Teacher Preparation Standards
history.description: Kansas adopted the standalone ESOL (K-6, 5-8, 6-12, PreK-12) Teacher Preparation Standards on 2017-05-09. These define the competency floor for the ESOL endorsement (the only EL credential offered in Kansas, as an add-on to a primary license).
